wish: someone should make a tool that tells a file's real type from its content, not its extension
spec:
Reads the first bytes of any file you drop and names its real format from magic numbers (about 100 formats, incl. docx/xlsx/apk inside ZIPs and old Office files) and text sniffing.
Drop or pick one or more files, or paste the first bytes as hex; each result says the real type, MIME, and whether the extension matches.
It does not upload anything, repair or rename files, or identify encrypted or headerless raw data.
notes: Reads only the first 64 kB of each file, locally. File-picker path cannot be exercised by verify steps, so tests use the hex paste input, which runs the same detector.
